How Much Does Professional Upholstery Cleaning Cost? 2026 Latest Prices

October 18, 2024
Table of Contents

If you are hoping to get your furniture looking good as new, you should find a great upholstery cleaningcompany. You are probably wondering “How much does upholstery cleaning cost?”

Upholstery cleaning costscan range in prices depending on what type of upholstery you need cleaned and how large the furniture is. A quick upholstery cleaning price listlooks something like this:

  • Office Chairs = $20 to $40
  • Ottoman = $20 to $50
  • Recliner or armchair = $60 to $80
  • Love Seat = $60 to $120
  • Small couch = $60 to $70
  • Full Sofa = $100 to $200

These figures show you what you can expect to pay for professional upholstery cleaning costs, but they don’t tell the whole story of what you will end up paying. There are lots more facts to understand about the cost for upholstery cleaning, so you should read this helpful guide to learn all you can.

Why Choose Upholstery Cleaning?

Having your beloved furniture’s upholstery cleaned by professionals will help it to last for many more years looking almost new. You paid good money for your furniture, and you should do your best to preserve it so that you can enjoy it for as long as possible.

Upholstery Cleaning Cost Factors

What you pay for professional upholstery cleaning depends on a few key things:

Furniture Material

Delicate silk or leather needs special care from a pro, which costs more. Hardy microfiber is cheaper to clean. Natural fibers like cotton may need low-moisture methods. Synthetics can handle deeper cleaning. Prices range from $100 for microfiber up to $500 for leather sofas.

Furniture Condition

If the fabric is older or has heavy, set-in stains, more work is required. Weak spots need gentler methods too. These factors mean getting custom treatment, for an added price.

Professional Upholstery Cleaning Method

Professionals choose the best process for your fabric, whether deep cleaning with steam or gentle dry foam. The right chemistry and technique matters. A pro analyzes each material and stain to determine what cleaning type brings the best results, keeping prices reasonable.

Labor

The time and effort it takes to fully clean a piece impacts prices. Larger upholstered items like sectionals, armchairs, and headboards naturally demand more labor and solutions to treat the expansive fabric, with more cushion and crevice areas. Expect to pay at least $30 more per additional piece of substantial size.

Type of Furniture

Prices fluctuate based on the particular upholstered item. Dining chairs average $25-$50 for a set versus $150+ for oversized reclining chairs. Heavily padded couches tend to cost over $200 depending on fabric and size, especially L-shaped designs. Antique fainting couches may run $300+ for delicate deep cleaning while basic armless chairs average under $100.

Additional Costs to Consider

While cleaning quotes mainly depend on your fabric and furniture size, extra services can take your pieces to the next level. Common add-ons to estimate into your budget include:

Stain Removal

Tough, set-in stains often warrant extra work and specific stain removal solutions. Expect an additional fee around $20 per substantial stain. Particularly difficult stains like wine or pet accidents may cost slightly more if intensive treatments are necessary.

Protective Treatments

Upholstery pros may recommend applying a stain-blocking solution after cleaning to help resist future stains. This protective application typically adds $20 to $30 per furniture piece to the bill but helps safeguard your investment between professional cleanings.

Repairs

If weaknesses in fabric are uncovered during cleaning, repairs may be suggested. Costs vary dramatically based on the repair type needed and extent of damage being fixed. Resewing detached cushion piping starts around $55 while full upholstery restoration work runs $200+. Discuss options with pros if issues surface.

Sanitization

For furniture exposed to biological contaminants like pet urine, skin oils or mold, sanitization adds $25 to $50 per piece. This intensive disinfecting of cushion interiors and lower fabric layers is well worth the investment for health and odor removal.

Ask providers to outline any added costs upfront so you can approve supplementary services as needed.

Should You DIY or Call the Experts?

Tackling upholstery yourself seems like a money saver. However, taking on delicate fabrics without the right tools can permanently damage pieces. And you want those expensive custom sofas or heirloom chairs lasting for years, right?

Most households lack the powerful suction cleaners, steamers, specialty solvents, and intensive stain solutions the pros rely on. Harsh DIY chemicals strip protective fabric treatments. Excess moisture causes mold blooms or dye bleeds. Lack of specialty training makes it easier to overlook weaknesses in material too.

Then if you do ruin the integrity of fabric or underlying cushions, repairs or full reupholstery replace the initial savings with a painful furniture bill.

Furniture that does not get regular upholstery cleaning will have to be thrown away much too soon in its lifecycle. Furniture is bulky and takes up a lot of space in a landfill after you are done with it, so it is important to keep it in good shape for as long as you can.

Upholstery cleaning will make your furniture look so good that you will forget how old it is. It will get rid of all kinds of stains and odors so that you can always feel good using your furniture and looking at it to decorate your home.

Will Upholstery Cleaners Come to My Home?

Many upholstery cleanersmake house calls because they understand that it is not easy to lug a giant couch in to be cleaned. They have mobile equipment that can be used in your home and do a wonderful job of getting your upholstery clean.

For smaller items, like a chair, the upholstery cleaner near you might even offer a discount if you bring the item into their shop. They will be saving time and resources by not having to travel to you, so you should get a discount in this case.

Professional upholstery cleaners are competent in performing their duties in your house in a safe and efficient manner. They will know exactly how to deal with your furniture and will be courteous to your home so that nothing is damaged while they are working.

What Is Included With Upholstery Cleaning

The typical upholstery cleaning servicestarts with an inspection of the furniture to see the best methods for cleaning. Cleaners need to use the right techniques based on the condition of your furniture.

The first part of cleaning is applying a heated cleaning solution to the upholstery that starts to loosen up any dirt or debris that is stuck in there. A professional cleaner uses special methods that don’t get the furniture too wet so it has an easy time drying.

Then the upholstery gets a good rinsing down with the upholstery cleaning want that sucks up moisture at the same time it is applied. This gets all of the loosened up dirt to come out so that the upholstery is left clean and beautiful.

Protective Solutions

Many professional upholstery cleaners will offer to add a stain blocking solution for an additional fee. The fee is usually small, something in the $20 to $30 range.

These protective solutions to a fantastic job of preventing damage that would require another visit by the upholstery cleaner. Some upholstery cleaning companies would rather you not choose to add the protective solution and hope you will be calling them again soon.

The protective solutions also help the fabric keep its color longer by blocking out rays from the sun. This will help to keep your furniture looking new for many more years than it would otherwise.

Which Stains Can Be Removed

A spill on a nice piece of furniture does not have to ruin it, professional upholstery cleaners can get rid of most stains with the right information. It is important that you tell your upholstery cleaning service what caused the stain and when it happened.

The sooner that you act to remove a stain the better. You can help by blotting up anything that falls onto your furniture, try not to rub stains because that can actually make them stick further into the upholstery fibers.

Some companies can charge extra for difficult stains, the fee should be in the $20 range. But for easy to remove stains the removal should be included with the normal upholstery cleaning fee.

Steam Cleaning Couch Cost

Having a steam cleaning for a couches upholstery is one of the preferred methods offered by many upholstery cleaning services. This method involves using a special machine that lifts dirt out of a couches fibers with a steam and vacuum wand.

You may think of renting a steam cleaning machine and do the job yourself. This can cost $40 to $60 for a full day rental which includes the shampoo and any materials you need.

It can be tricky for a first timer to steam clean a couch and the danger is that you can burn the upholstery and cause more damage. For a little bit more money, it is a lot easier to let the professionals take care of steam cleaning your couch.

How to Save Money on Upholstery Cleaning Costs

Upholstery care grabs a big bite of your home budget if you only call pros when stains are disastrous. But you can take steps to cut costs between deep cleanings:

  1. Vacuum frequently using the soft brush attachment to lift surface dirt before it settles in. Quick passes two times per week make professional cleaning less frequent.
  2. Spot clean spills ASAP by gently blotting moist messes or using a certified green cleaner for stubborn spots. This stops stains from settling into fabric or cushions.
  3. Compare area upholstery cleaner rates. Bigger retail franchises often cost more than local family shops for the same services.
  4. Ask what pre-treatments included in pricing do. Some providers classify essential pre-scrubbing as “add-ons” that let them lower the base price.
  5. Schedule low-season cleanings in slower winter months when reputable companies offer discounts to fill scheduling gaps.

Remember, cutting too many corners by skipping professional treatments altogether backfires over time. But staying consistently on top of care, shopping cleaning providers, and extending the time between deep treatments keeps your investment fresh.

How Often To Have Upholstery Cleaning Done

The frequency of upholstery cleaning you need will depend a lot on your lifestyle. If you live alone you will have different needs than if you have pets and children in your house.

A single person or couple can be comfortable with one upholstery cleaning per year. This will keep your furniture looking and smelling great.

If you have children or pets but not both, two times a year should be sufficient to keep you home looking good. If you have children and pets together, you may need to clean your upholstery three or four times per year because of all of the use it will see.
